newsitem.title: NORWAY: Derivatives trade at Oslo Bourse hits peak.
newsitem.headline: Derivatives trade at Oslo Bourse hits peak.

text.p: Trade in options and futures on the Oslo Stock Exchange reached its highest turnover on Thursday since the derivatives system became electronic and a link was set up to Stockholm and London, the bourse said on Thursday.
The new system, which links the tiny Oslo market to the Swedish derivatives exchange OM and its London equivalent OMLX, went on line on February 14.
"When the market closed at 5 p.m. (1500gmt), a total of 17,640 contracts had been traded, including 12,950 share options and 4,690 OBX options," Oslo Bourse said in a statement.
OBX is the top 25 share index measured by turnover.
Options in Kvaerner, the anglo-Norwegian construction and engineering group, amounted to 50 percent of total share option turnover, the statement said.
The share price has gone up since the company presented first-quarter profits last week that beat market expectations.
On April 8, the bourse said daily trade in options and futures had gone up by an average 90 and 100 percent respectively so far this year compared to 1996.
Trade in Oslo, one of Europe's smallest derivatives markets, has increased both in terms of liquidity, number of players and derivative papers available.

In 1996, Oslo handled an average of only 6,000 contracts a day in stock options/futures and interest futures. Since February 14, average trade has risen to about 9,000 contracts a day, according to the bourse.
Derivatives trade is mainly in stock options, which totals 10 companies.
